Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Apurva Prakash Tiwari,Ashwani Tripathi,Ramanuj Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing
the State.

By means of this bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. applicant -Vishal Jaysaval, who is
involved in Case Crime No. 202 of 2024 under sections 366, 376 I.P.C., Police Station Sarai Akil,
District Kaushambi
seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that as per F.I.R. version, allegation has been levelled that on 15.05.2024, at about 04:30 pm., victim was enticed away by the applicant.
Victim was recovered on 28.05.2024, thereafter her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., was recorded in which she has disclosed that she is a student of 12th standard and is aged about 18 years.

sentences.text: On 15.05.2024, applicant lured her and called her to Prayagraj Railway Station.
When she went there, he took her to Surat where he left her in the house of his relative and made physical relation with her.
Thereafter on 25.05.2024, she came from Surat to Mirzapur along with the applicant and thereafter she was recovered.

It is also pointed out that on 24.05.2024, victim and applicant solemnized marriage in Vindhyavasini Temple and also executed an affidavit in this regard which has been filed as Annexure No.10 to the affidavit.
On the strength of the aforesaid fact, it is argued that both are major and they were consenting party.
On the other hand, learned Additional Government Advocate vehemently opposed the prayer for bail but does not dispute the factum of the case as argued on behalf of the applicant.

Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, I find that victim has travelled from Prayagraj to Surat along with the applicant and she was in the company of applicant for thirteen days' but she did not make any assistance whereas she had an ample opportunity to raise alarm, therefore, possibility of victim being consenting party with the applicant cannot be ruled out and under the facts and material on record, this Court feels that the applicant has made out a case for grant of bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant-Vishal Jaysaval be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the applicant on bail.
In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the applicant.

Order Date :- 10.1.2025 NSC  Vishal Jaysaval vs State Of U.P. on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7866806/
